podcast.body: Appearing as a bonus track on the 12-inch single for "Where The Streets Have No Name," "Silver and Gold" originated as a contribution to the Artists Against Apartheid project. Its inclusion showcased U2's use of singles to release socially conscious or otherwise unreleased material. "Silver and Gold, which began life as a contribution to the artist against apartheid project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Digital Debris Part 1: B-Sides and Bonus Tracks

podcast.body: This track, considered a live favorite, was recorded for The Joshua Tree but ultimately cut because it "just wasn't done." An earlier version was co-written by Bono with Keith Richards and Ron Wood for the "Sun City" anti-apartheid collection, making a last-minute inclusion there. It was later rewritten and re-recorded during The Joshua Tree sessions, then became the second half of the B-side for the "Where the Streets Have No Name" single in 1987, alongside "The Sweetest Thing." "This song predated the Joshua Tree by about two years."
